$comment: RAY-CLOUD shared contract 1.0.0-rc.1. Stable error vocabulary. Codes are append-only; a code never changes meaning, exit code or retryable flag within a contract major.

exitCodes.meaning: completed; the verdict is negative (existing meaning of doctor, plan and deploy refusals)

exitRule: ok true exits 0 and has no errors. ok false has at least one error; the process exits with the exit code of the error class that comes first in exitPrecedence among all errors present. A retryable exit (5) is reported only when no other class is present. Warnings never change the exit code.
errorOrderRule: errors[0] is the first failing check in the pipeline order defined for the verb; later entries are further findings of the same or later checks. Golden fixture expectations compare errors[0].code and errors[0].reason.

codes.meaning: The command line is invalid: unknown verb or flag, missing or malformed argument, conflicting flags, or a --deployment id that differs from the state directory or the database; or the source of an export holds no organization.
codes.action: Fix the command line; see the verb help.

codes.meaning: An unexpected internal error. No partial result may be trusted; the message carries no stack or secret.
codes.action: Report it with the operationId; do not retry blindly.

codes.meaning: An existing verb completed and its verdict is negative for a reason that has no typed code yet; the legacy message is carried verbatim in message. A bundle deploy reports the same code when the boot of the version it applied refuses its configuration, with the boot reason as message.
codes.action: Read the message; fix the input.

codes.meaning: The file is not a .ray in the strict v1 container profile.
codes.action: Rebuild the bundle with a conforming writer.

codes.meaning: A byte, entry, path, nesting, time or CPU budget was exceeded while reading or writing. object-index-size is an object index larger than the migration extracted limit, or a blob root of more than 500,000 objects (the most an object index holds).
codes.action: Reduce the input; limits may only be lowered by configuration.

codes.meaning: A declared size or digest does not match the bytes, or clear outer metadata disagrees with authenticated inner metadata.
codes.action: Treat the artifact as corrupt or forged; obtain it again from its source.

codes.meaning: ray.json, snapshot.json, the object index or a managed receipt is not canonical JSON, fails its JSON Schema, or breaks a semantic rule.
codes.action: Rebuild the bundle; the path field names the offending member.

codes.meaning: The spec inside a bundle does not parse; the SPEC_ codes in the same errors list give the detail.
codes.action: Fix the spec and pack again.

codes.meaning: pack could not build a sealed closure: unresolved import, a link escaping the closure, an excluded file class, or a native module without a validated linux/x64 build.
codes.action: Fix the closure or the inclusion list; pack never copies local node_modules silently.

codes.meaning: pack found no application id or version: neither the spec metadata nor --id/--version gives a value, or the value does not match the manifest pattern.
codes.action: Add metadata.id and metadata.version to the spec, or pass --id and --version.

codes.meaning: The output path exists and --force was not given, or the output would be written as plaintext where only encrypted output is allowed.
codes.action: Choose another path or pass --force where the verb allows it.

codes.meaning: A detached provenance signature is malformed, does not verify, or was made by a key that is not trusted.
codes.action: Do not deploy; obtain a correctly signed bundle or approve it through quarantine.

codes.meaning: The requested exact runtime version is not this runtime, is not in the signed release catalog, or an extension declares an @rayspec/* range that excludes it.
codes.action: Use a bundle built for this runtime, or deploy on the runtime the bundle pins.

codes.meaning: The bundle target (os, arch, Node major) or the snapshot database major is not supported by this runtime.
codes.action: Use a supported target.

codes.meaning: A required capability id is unknown to the vocabulary or not provided by this runtime, or the requested execution level is not available.
codes.action: Deploy on a runtime that provides it, or remove the requirement.

codes.meaning: The bundle declares or the bindings file supplies a reserved operator name.
codes.action: Rename the application binding; reserved names come only from the operator.

codes.meaning: A required binding has no value at deploy or apply time.
codes.action: Supply it in the bindings file or the explicit environment.

codes.meaning: The bindings, identity or key file is a link, not a regular file, not owned by the invoking user, or readable or writable by group or others; or the deployment state directory is a link, not owned by the invoking user, or not mode 0700.
codes.action: chmod 600 the file (0700 the state directory) and pass a regular file.

codes.meaning: pack or verify found a value that looks like a credential inside the closure.
codes.action: Remove the secret from the payload and declare a binding instead.

codes.meaning: The bundle needs a product schema change that the plan does not approve, or the target schema head is not the one the bundle migrates from.
codes.action: Prepare a plan with the reviewed delta and allowlist.

codes.meaning: The product delta regenerated from the live schema and the new spec differs from the delta carried in the bundle.
codes.action: Rebuild the bundle against the live schema head.

codes.meaning: The live product schema does not match any known schema head (drift found by introspection).
codes.action: Reconcile the schema manually before any apply or export.

codes.meaning: The plan expired or an input covered by the plan digest changed since prepare.
codes.action: Run prepare again and review the new plan.

codes.meaning: An idempotency key was reused with a different plan digest or request.
codes.action: Use a new idempotency key for a different request.

codes.meaning: The shared schema advisory lock was not acquired within the bounded wait, or another operation holds the environment's operation lease.
codes.action: Retry later with the same idempotency key.

codes.meaning: A dependency (database, blob storage, disk) is unreachable or temporarily failing.
codes.action: Retry with backoff and the same idempotency key.

codes.meaning: Import target is not empty: it has platform or product rows, blobs or a non-initial schema head.
codes.action: Import only into a new empty target; no in-place merge.

codes.meaning: The source could not be fenced before the deadline, or the fence was lost before the snapshot completed.
codes.action: The source stays fenced; retry quiesce or resume the source explicitly.

codes.meaning: The fence epoch in the request does not match the active fence, or the lease the operation held on the environment expired or was taken over, so it may not write.
codes.action: Use the epoch returned by quiesce; after a lost lease, run the operation again.

codes.meaning: The source has state the export cannot capture consistently: uncontrolled external database writers, an unsupported blob adapter, pending non-replayable external effects, a table that is neither a platform table nor a product store, or no database write barrier the application cannot bypass.
codes.action: Reconcile or remove the external state, or enable database role separation (or stop the source and attest it), then retry precheck.

codes.meaning: The source holds more than one application tenant (organization); v1 snapshots carry exactly one.
codes.action: Export is not available for this deployment in v1.

codes.meaning: An organization would have no way back in after import: no active member of it holds a password, and the import resets every API key, session and invite.
codes.action: Add a password-holding owner before export. On the target, an owner without a password is let back in with rayspec tenant recover-owner.

codes.meaning: The age ciphertext could not be decrypted with the given identity, or failed authentication. Nothing was imported.
codes.action: Check the identity file; obtain the artifact again.

codes.meaning: An operator or platform policy refused the operation: a plan with blockers, an apply while the environment is fenced, a dump with privileged statements, an unsupported extension or an unmapped owner, or a refused grant or posture.
codes.action: Change the request or have the policy owner approve it.

codes.meaning: The operation was interrupted (SIGINT or SIGTERM). Any fence it took stays held.
codes.action: Follow the recovery instruction in the message: resume the source when a fence was taken, otherwise run the command again.

codes.meaning: A crash or failure left a step in an unknown state; automatic replay is not safe.
codes.action: Inspect the receipts and reconcile manually.

warnings.meaning: The bundle has no detached provenance signature. Under the managed posture it may only enter quarantine and be approved explicitly by an authorized deployer; a local self-host deploy accepts it with this warning unless --require-signature is given.
The product schema head was computed by introspection because no product migration ledger exists yet.
The spec uses an agent backend or speech provider but declares no egress hosts; host network policy will deny its calls.
quiesce cannot fence named external services; they are listed in the result.
An existing verb ran with --json; data carries its legacy result object unchanged.

specCodeMapping.rule: A spec error or warning appears in the envelope with code "SPEC_" followed by its spec code in upper case (for example yaml_parse_error becomes SPEC_YAML_PARSE_ERROR), its path unchanged and retryable false. Every mapped error has exit 1. The mapping is total and mechanical, so a spec code appended later maps without a contract change. SPEC_ codes are never reused for anything else.
